Kovel New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Volynska oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. This is the newer of Kovel's Jewish cemeteries. Jews settled in Kovel from the early 16th century, gaining the right to reside on all streets in 1614; Rabbi Mordechai of Neskhizh's relocation from Toykut, documented elsewhere in this collection, brought Trisk, Neskhizh, and Ruzhin Hasidism to the city, which supported 13 synagogues by 1910. The Jewish population reached 8,521 by 1897 and 12,758 by 1921, with Jews holding half the city's municipal administration seats during the interwar period; noted politician Chaim Pazner (1899–1981) was a resident. Following the June 1941 occupation, two ghettos held about 24,000 Jews, with 8,600 murdered in a single action on June 3–5, 1942. This cemetery, estimated founded in the mid-to-late 19th century, was the site of around 5,000 shootings in August 1942; damaged during WWII, it was demolished in 1970, its tombstones used for road construction at a nearby military base.
